question: Is wine Vegan?
answer: Not always. Some wines are filtered with animal products like gelatin, egg whites or fish bladder (isinglass). Look for wines labeled Vegan, or check the winery's site.
notes: Everyday Vegan question, written by Logan 2026-10-06

question: Is sugar Vegan?
answer: Usually, but not always. Some white cane sugar is filtered through bone char. Beet sugar, organic sugar and sugar labeled Vegan are not processed that way.
notes: Everyday Vegan question, written by Logan 2026-10-06

question: Is gelatin Vegan?
answer: No. Gelatin is made from animal skin and bones. Look for agar agar, pectin or products labeled Vegan instead, especially in gummies, marshmallows and desserts.
notes: Everyday Vegan question, written by Logan 2026-10-06

question: Are eggs Vegan?
answer: No. Vegans leave out eggs. For baking, try a flax egg (1 tablespoon ground flaxseed and 3 tablespoons water), mashed banana or a store-bought egg replacer. For scrambles, tofu or a plant-based egg works well.
also_asked: what can i use instead of eggs
notes: Everyday Vegan question, written by Logan 2026-10-06

question: What can I use instead of dairy milk?
answer: Oat, soy, almond, coconut and pea milk are all easy swaps. Oat and soy work well in coffee, and soy has the most protein.
notes: Everyday Vegan question, written by Logan 2026-10-06

question: What do Vegans use instead of cheese?
answer: There are cheeses made from cashews, almonds, coconut and soy, and they melt well on pizza and grilled cheese. Nutritional yeast adds a cheesy flavor to sauces and popcorn.
notes: Everyday Vegan question, written by Logan 2026-10-06

question: Where do Vegans get protein?
answer: Beans, lentils, tofu, tempeh, seitan, edamame, nuts, seeds and whole grains are all good sources. Eating a variety through the day covers most people's needs.
notes: Everyday Vegan question, written by Logan 2026-10-06

question: Do Vegans need vitamin B12?
answer: Yes. B12 is the one nutrient Vegans should plan for, through fortified foods or a supplement. Talk with your doctor about what is right for you.
notes: Everyday Vegan question, written by Logan 2026-10-06

question: What is the difference between Vegan and vegetarian?
answer: Vegetarians leave out meat and fish but may eat eggs, dairy and honey. Vegans leave out all animal products, and many also avoid them in clothing and other products.
notes: Everyday Vegan question, written by Logan 2026-10-06

question: What does plant-based mean?
answer: Plant-based usually describes food made from plants, with no animal products. Vegan goes further, covering how people live beyond food too, like clothing and products.
notes: Everyday Vegan question, written by Logan 2026-10-06

question: How do I start going Vegan?
answer: Start with meals you already like and swap one thing at a time: plant milk, a Vegan burger, a bean chili. Your Guide and the guides can help, and the Directory shows Vegan spots near you.
notes: Everyday Vegan question, written by Logan 2026-10-06

question: What are easy Vegan swaps for comfort food?
answer: Try plant-based burgers and sausages, Vegan mac and cheese with cashew sauce, jackfruit for pulled pork, and coconut or oat ice cream. Most comfort food has a Vegan version.

what are easy vegan swaps for my favorite comfort foods
notes: Everyday Vegan question, written by Logan 2026-10-06

question: How do I eat Vegan at a non-Vegan restaurant?
answer: Check the menu online first, look for dishes you can adjust, and ask for no butter, cheese or cream. Many restaurants are happy to help. The Directory shows Vegan-friendly spots with Vegan options.
notes: Everyday Vegan question, written by Logan 2026-10-06

question: Is Vegan food expensive?
answer: It doesn't have to be. Beans, lentils, rice, pasta, oats, frozen vegetables and seasonal produce are some of the cheapest foods there are. Specialty products cost more, so treat them as extras.
notes: Everyday Vegan question, written by Logan 2026-10-06

question: Is leather Vegan?
answer: No. Leather comes from animal skin. Vegans choose alternatives like plant-based leathers, cotton, canvas and recycled materials.
notes: Everyday Vegan question, written by Logan 2026-10-06

question: Is wool or silk Vegan?
answer: No. Wool comes from sheep and silk from silkworms. Cotton, linen, hemp and recycled fibers are common Vegan choices.
notes: Everyday Vegan question, written by Logan 2026-10-06

question: What is tofu, and how do I cook it?
answer: Tofu is made from soybeans and takes on whatever flavor you give it. Press out the water, cut it up, season it, then bake, pan-fry or air-fry until golden.
notes: Everyday Vegan question, written by Logan 2026-10-06

question: What is seitan?
answer: Seitan is made from wheat gluten and has a chewy, meaty texture. It is high in protein and great in stir-fries, sandwiches and stews. It is not for anyone avoiding gluten.
notes: Everyday Vegan question, written by Logan 2026-10-06

question: What is tempeh?
answer: Tempeh is fermented soybeans pressed into a firm block, with a nutty flavor and lots of protein. Slice it thin and marinate it for sandwiches, bowls and stir-fries.
notes: Everyday Vegan question, written by Logan 2026-10-06

question: Are Vegan meat alternatives healthy?
answer: They can be part of a good diet, and they make swapping easier. Like any packaged food, check the label for sodium. Whole foods like beans, lentils and tofu are great everyday staples.
notes: Everyday Vegan question, written by Logan 2026-10-06

question: Can kids be Vegan?
answer: Yes, with planning, and many families raise Vegan kids. Work with your pediatrician to make sure they get enough B12, iron, calcium, vitamin D and omega-3s.
notes: Everyday Vegan question, written by Logan 2026-10-06

question: Can athletes be Vegan?
answer: Yes. Many athletes and bodybuilders are Vegan. Plan for enough calories and protein from beans, tofu, tempeh, seitan and protein powders. The Vegans Who Lift Podcast covers it in depth.
notes: Everyday Vegan question, written by Logan 2026-10-06

question: Is chocolate Vegan?
answer: Dark chocolate often is, but check the label for milk, milk fat or butterfat. Many brands make Vegan milk-style chocolate with oat or rice milk.
notes: Everyday Vegan question, written by Logan 2026-10-06

question: Is bread Vegan?
answer: Most bread is, but some has milk, eggs, butter or honey. Check the label, or ask at the bakery. The Directory lists Vegan bakeries near you.
notes: Everyday Vegan question, written by Logan 2026-10-06

question: What are good honey alternatives?
answer: Maple syrup, agave, date syrup and brown rice syrup all work well in tea, baking and dressings.
also_asked: what can i use instead of honey
notes: Everyday Vegan question, written by Logan 2026-10-06

question: Are Vegan cosmetics different from cruelty-free?
answer: Yes. Cruelty-free means not tested on animals. Vegan means no animal ingredients, like beeswax, lanolin or carmine. Look for products that are both.
notes: Everyday Vegan question, written by Logan 2026-10-06

question: How do I talk to family about going Vegan?
answer: Lead with why it matters to you, keep it positive, and share good food. Offering to bring a dish to family meals helps a lot. Your Guide can help you find recipes everyone will enjoy.
notes: Everyday Vegan question, written by Logan 2026-10-06

question: What should I eat for a quick Vegan breakfast?
answer: Oatmeal with fruit and nut butter, a tofu scramble, avocado toast, a smoothie with plant milk and protein powder, or overnight oats are all quick and filling.
notes: Everyday Vegan question, written by Logan 2026-10-06

question: How do I find Vegan catering?
answer: Search the Directory for your city and look under Food and Services for Vegan caterers and chefs. You can also ask in your city's Community Board for recommendations.
